messages.label: scam
messages.text: GOV.UK HMRC Notice: Our records show an overpayment of £412.18 from the 2025/26 tax year. Funds will be returned once you verify your account here [link] Ref: [number]
messages.note: HMRC never contacts people by text about money owed back; link harvests bank details.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Royal Mail: we were unable to complete your delivery as the postcode on the item is incomplete. To avoid it being returned to sender please confirm a new slot: [link]
messages.note: Unsolicited missed-delivery text with a link to a fake courier page.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: hey mum its me, dropped my phone down the loo last night so using this one for now. are you about? need to ask you something x
messages.note: Hard: unknown number claiming to be a child, no ask yet; classic opener before a money request.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Caller: Good afternoon, am I speaking with the account holder? I'm ringing from Barclays security team. Someone's just tried to set up a new payee on your account from a device in Manchester. Your current account is compromised, so we've opened a protected holding account for you — I'll talk you through moving your balance across now, and if anyone from the branch asks, just say it's to a relative.
messages.note: Caller posing as bank pushes transfer to a 'protected' account and a cover story.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Dear Motorist, we were unable to process your most recent vehicle tax payment as your billing information has expired. Please reconfirm your card within 48 hours to prevent enforcement action and possible clamping of your vehicle. Login here: [link] — DVLA Customer Services
messages.note: Fake DVLA email asking to confirm card details via a link.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: PCN Notice: A penalty charge of £60 has been issued to your vehicle for overstaying at a pay & display car park on 12/11. Settle within 3 days or the charge rises to £120 and will be passed to debt recovery. [link]
messages.note: Unsolicited parking penalty text with payment link; real PCNs come by post.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Hiya, it's Jan from the school PTA chat. Sorry to bother you! Just sorting the list for Thursday's online meeting, you should've had a text with some numbers in it from WhatsApp, can you pop it back to me so I can add you? Thanks so much
messages.note: Hard: friendly group member asking for the WhatsApp registration code, which hands over the account.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Hi there! I'm Chloe, HR assistant at a UK digital agency. Your CV was passed to us. We have remote positions helping merchants boost app ratings, about an hour a day, daily pay of £120-£350. Interested? Add our coordinator on WhatsApp [number]
messages.note: Unsolicited remote 'task' job offer moving to WhatsApp, leads to paying to unlock tasks.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Hi yes the PS5 is still yours if you want it. I'm away with work in Aberdeen till the end of the month so can't do collection, but I can get it couriered tomorrow morning. Easiest if you send the £180 by bank transfer tonight and I'll send tracking, cheers
messages.note: Hard: polite seller with an excuse not to meet, cheap price, bank transfer only.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Automated voice: This is an urgent message from Her Majesty's tax office. Due to an unpaid balance, a case has been registered under your name and enforcement officers will attend your address within 24 hours. To settle this matter and stop the warrant, stay on the line and an officer will take your payment.
messages.note: Robocall impersonating HMRC threatening arrest/enforcement unless you pay now.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Student Loans Company: We were unable to release your Term 1 instalment because your bank information could not be verified. To avoid delays to your funding please update your details via your secure portal [link] within 24 hours.
messages.note: Phishing email timed around loan payments asking to update bank details via link.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Gov.UK: Pensioners entitled to the £200-£300 heating allowance must register their details by Friday or the payment for this winter will not be made. Register now: [link]
messages.note: Winter Fuel Payment is automatic; text asks pensioners to 'register' via a link.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: [number] is your Monzo verification code. Never share this code with anyone, not even Monzo. If you didn't request it, ignore this message.
messages.note: Genuine one-time code that explicitly says not to share it; no link or ask.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Evri: Your parcel from ASOS will be delivered today between 13:10 and 14:10. Your courier is Dave. Track in the Evri app.
messages.note: Real delivery update for an expected order, no payment or details requested.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Mum can you lend me £40 till Friday? Car insurance came out early and I'm short for the train pass. Will pay you back when I get paid, same as last time. Is Dad still coming Sunday for the roast?
messages.note: Relative's usual number, specific personal context, small loan, no urgency or new number.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Your Self Assessment tax return for the year ending 5 April 2026 is due by 31 January. To file or check what you owe, sign in to your HMRC online account or the HMRC app. We will never ask for your bank details by email.
messages.note: Government reminder with no link, tells you to log in yourself via the official app/site.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Mate have you seen this?? The council are finally fixing the potholes on our road lol [link]
messages.note: Friend sharing a news article link from their known number, nothing asked.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Hi all, reminder that timesheets need to be submitted in the usual system by 5pm today or payroll won't process them this month. Ping me if you're stuck. Thanks, Priya
messages.note: Urgent but routine internal work message, no link, no money or credentials.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Thanks for your order! Order #[number] — 1 x kettle, 2 x mugs. Total paid £47.97. We'll email you again when it ships. You can view your order any time in your account.
messages.note: Ordinary shop order confirmation for something already bought.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Reminder: you have an appointment at Riverside Surgery with the practice nurse on Tue 18 Nov at 10:40. If you can't attend please call the surgery to cancel. Reply not required.
messages.note: Standard NHS GP appointment reminder, no link or payment.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Hiya it's Tom from five-a-side, got a new phone on a different network so this is my new number. Delete the old one. See you Weds
messages.note: Friend announcing a new number and asking for nothing.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Hi, is the bike still available? Does it come with the lights in the photo? I could pick up Saturday morning and pay cash if that's ok
messages.note: Normal marketplace buyer question, offers to collect in person and pay cash.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Caller: Hello, is that Margaret? Please don't be alarmed, this is Detective Constable Reynolds from the Metropolitan Police fraud squad. We've arrested two men using cloned cards and one had your details. We believe someone at your local branch is involved, so I must ask you not to discuss this with staff. Would you be willing to assist us? It would mean drawing out some cash tomorrow, and an officer will collect it from your home in a sealed evidence bag.
messages.note: Hard: fake police officer sets up an 'operation' where a courier collects the victim's cash.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Sponsored · WATCH before it's taken down: the TV money expert everyone trusts finally admits how he tops up his pension. A government-approved platform turning £250 into a steady weekly income for ordinary Britons. Spaces close tonight. [link]
messages.note: Sponsored video ad with a faked trusted presenter pushing an investment platform.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Dear Customer, Ref [number]. Following our investigation into an unauthorised trading platform, the Financial Conduct Authority has identified you as an affected investor and secured £6,830 on your behalf. Before funds can be released, a compliance clearance fee of £395 must be settled. Reply to this email to receive payment instructions. FCA Recovery Desk
messages.note: Fake regulator claims to have recovered lost money and asks for a release fee.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Hey! Saw you liked our post about student side income 😊 We're a small payments firm and we need people to receive customer payments into their account and pass them on, you keep 10% of each one. Takes 5 mins a day. Do you bank with Monzo or Starling? Just need your sort code, account number and a pic of your ID to set you up.
messages.note: Easy-money 'job' asking for bank details and ID to move money through the victim's account.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Caller: Hiya, it's Gary, you put a post on the village group about a leaky gutter? I'm local so I drove past this morning, and to be honest it's not just the gutter, your chimney flashing's gone as well. That's normally £1,800 but if you can do half in cash up front today I'll get the lads on it this afternoon before the rain comes in.
messages.note: Hard: friendly local trader inflates the job and wants cash up front the same day.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Morning beautiful ☀️ I hardly slept, kept thinking about our chat last night. The signal on the rig is awful so video still won't work, I'm so sorry. Two more months and I'm home and we can finally have that walk on the beach. There's something I need to ask you tonight but I'm a bit embarrassed x
messages.note: Hard: online partner who can never video call, building up to a money request.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Got 2 standing tickets for Saturday's sold-out gig, my mate's dropped out. £85 each, what I paid. PayPal's playing up so bank transfer only and I'll email them straight over once it lands. Message me on WhatsApp [number], few people asking so first come first served
messages.note: Spare tickets for a sold-out event, moved to WhatsApp, bank transfer only.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: HM Revenue & Customs: You have an unclaimed tax rebate of £267.40. Claims must be made within 5 working days or the amount will be forfeited. Complete the short form and enter the debit card you would like the funds credited to: [link]
messages.note: Fake HMRC refund email asking for card details via a link.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: DPD: Your parcel is being held at our depot due to an unpaid redelivery fee of £1.45. Pay today to rebook, otherwise the item will be returned to the sender. [link]
messages.note: Small 'redelivery fee' text with a link to steal card details.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Hi dad it's me, this is my new number, old one's completely dead. Sorry to ask but I need to pay for the new phone and a bill today and my banking app won't work until it's set up on here. Could you transfer £680 for me? I'll send you the details, will pay you back Friday x
messages.note: Unknown number claiming to be a child, asks for money to someone else's account.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Lloyds: Did you attempt a payment of £948.00 to JB TRADING LTD? If NOT, call our fraud team immediately on [number]. Do not reply to this message.
messages.note: Hard: fake fraud alert gives its own number to call, which leads to the 'safe account' con.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Hi, it's Sarah from Pilates! Sorry, I'm locked out of my WhatsApp and it's sending the code to your phone because I put you down as my backup. Could you forward me the 6 digits? Need it before tonight's class chat 🙏
messages.note: Hard: group contact asks for a WhatsApp code, which hands over the account.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Great work today! You've completed 38 of 40 tasks 🎉 To finish the set your account needs a top-up of £75, which is returned along with your £412 commission tonight. Send a screenshot once it's done and your mentor will unlock the last two.
messages.note: Later stage of a task-job scam: pay in to 'unlock' tasks and earnings.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Yes still available, brand new still in the box. It was a gift and I already have one so letting it go cheap at £220. I'm in Cornwall so can't meet but I'll post it recorded delivery. If you pay via PayPal friends and family I'll send it today, cheers
messages.note: Hard: seller can't meet, underpriced item, insists on payment with no buyer protection.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Student Finance England: Action required. Your maintenance loan for the spring term is on hold because we need to verify your identity. Sign in within 24 hours to avoid your payments being suspended: [link]
messages.note: Fake student loan email with a deadline and a login link.

messages.label: scam
messages.text: Caller: Hello, I'm calling from HMRC's compliance department about unpaid tax from 2023. A warrant has been prepared and officers can attend your address today. To stop this, the outstanding £1,140 must be settled now on this call. Don't hang up and don't speak to anyone else, this call is recorded.
messages.note: Fake HMRC caller threatens arrest and demands immediate payment.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: We've temporarily blocked your debit card ending [number] after an unusual payment attempt. To unblock it, check the alert in your banking app or call us on the number on the back of your card. We will never ask you to move money or tell us your PIN.
messages.note: Genuine card block that points to the app and the number on the card.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Royal Mail: Sorry we missed you today. Your parcel will be at your local delivery office from tomorrow after 2pm. Bring the card we left and photo ID. No payment is needed.
messages.note: Real missed-delivery notice: no link, no fee.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Hi love, it's Dad. The plumber's just finished the boiler and wants £120 cash and I've only got £60 on me. Any chance you could send the rest to my usual Nationwide account? I'll sort you out at Sunday lunch
messages.note: From Dad's saved number with real context; a normal family request.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: 🎉 GIVEAWAY 🎉 To celebrate 5 years of the bakery we're giving away a cake for 6! Just follow us and tag a friend below. Winner picked Friday and announced here, then pop in to collect. We'll never ask for card details.
messages.note: Shop's own giveaway: no payment and no personal data.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Dear parents and carers, due to a burst water main the school will close at 12:30 today. Please arrange collection as soon as possible. Updates will follow on the school app. Thank you for your understanding.
messages.note: Urgent school closure notice with no link or payment.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Your NHS App security code is [number]. Do not share this code with anyone. If you did not try to log in, you can ignore this message.
messages.note: Genuine one-time code that says not to share it.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Hi Lucy, just confirming rent stays at £950 from December as we agreed when you renewed. Same standing order, nothing to change your end. Shout if the boiler plays up again. Thanks, Mark
messages.note: Landlord confirming agreed rent with no change of payment details.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Hiya, it's Sophie! New phone and new number, the old one finally died. No need to reply, just save this one. See you at Emma's on Saturday x
messages.note: Friend's new number message that asks for nothing.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Hi, interested in the sofa. Could you tell me the measurements and whether it'll fit through a normal door? I'd bring a van and pay cash on collection.
messages.note: Normal buyer questions, collecting and paying in person.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Your vehicle tax runs out at the end of this month. You can tax your vehicle online on GOV.UK or at a Post Office. You'll need your reminder letter or your log book. DVLA will never text you asking for payment.
messages.note: Government reminder telling you to go to the site yourself.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: URGENT: everyone must complete the mandatory fire safety module on the learning portal by 5pm Friday. Log in through the intranet as usual. Managers will chase anyone outstanding on Monday. Thanks, HR
messages.note: Employer deadline with urgency but no payment or data request.

messages.label: safe
messages.text: Octopus Energy: Your monthly direct debit is changing from £96 to £104 from 1 December, based on your usage. No action needed. You can see the details in your online account.
messages.note: Real supplier notice with no link or request.
